<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard AUR package for an Nginx module sourced from a Git repository. During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, the only executed code is at the top level and within `pkgver()`. The `source` array uses a `git+https` URL pointing to the project's own GitHub repository, which is expected and safe. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is normal for VCS packages and does not pose a risk during source download, as no execution occurs.

The `pkgver()` function runs `git rev-list` and `git rev-parse` on the cloned repository to generate a revision-based version string. These are safe, read-only operations on the local Git repo metadata. There is no command substitution, network access, or data exfiltration in the global scope or `pkgver()`. All potentially dangerous functions (`prepare`, `build`, `package`) are skipped due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags and are out of scope for this gate.

No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized actions occur during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD. The operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for git-based packages.
</details>

The PKGBUILD file is a standard Arch User Repository (AUR) package recipe for building the `ngx_dynamic_etag` Nginx module from source via Git. It follows typical AUR packaging practices: it clones the upstream Git repository, configures the build using Nginx's build system with appropriate flags, compiles the module, and installs the resulting shared object files and license into the package directory.

The use of `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is expected and normal for Git sources, as the content is mutable and checksums cannot be pinned. This does not indicate malice. The build process uses symbolic links to the installed `nginx-mainline-src` tree, which is a legitimate method for building dynamic modules against the main Nginx source. There are no network operations at build time beyond the initial Git clone defined in `source`, no obfuscated code, and no suspicious file or system manipulations.

All operations are confined to building and packaging a dynamic Nginx module. The package installs only the compiled module and its license, with no post-install scripts or system modifications. The maintainer metadata and URLs point to a legitimate GitHub repository. No evidence of supply-chain attack or malicious behavior is present.
</details>
